Single atomic commit prefix: feat(audio): KindAudio + Telegram voice handler stores .ogg (US-MM-A01)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: read internal/telegram/documents.go (270+ LOC, the template) AND internal/telegram/handlers.go (the registration site) AND internal/telegram/bot.go (the Bot struct + NewBot) AND internal/telegram/setup.go (the wiring) AND internal/storage/sources/store/{source.go, formats.go, store.go} (the source schema + PutInput signature). The docHandler shape IS the template — do NOT invent a new pattern, copy + adapt. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this story does NOT touch whisper client, does NOT call /inference, does NOT write transcript.txt — those are US-MM-A02. Status after process() success in A01 is StatusStored (default after Put — no Update call needed). The StatusTranscribeComplete constant is ADDED in A01 but not yet SET by any code path; A02 wires the Update call. Audio voice messages from Telegram are tele.Voice objects accessed via c.Message().Voice (NOT c.Message().Audio — Audio is a separate update type for music files; Voice is the recorded-on-device memo type). Voice has fields: File (embedded), Duration (seconds), MIMEType. We use voice.File for download and ignore voice.Duration / voice.MIMEType in A01 — A02 may store voice.Duration in the source.json TranscriptMeta. progressEditor helper exists in documents.go-adjacent files (grep for `newProgressEditor` — it's in internal/telegram/progress.go or similar; reuse it). Concurrency limit = 1 because (a) voice memos average <60s = quick turnaround, (b) whisper sidecar can only handle 1 inference at a time efficiently on 4-thread mini-PC. DO NOT register .ogg in formatsByExt — tele.OnVoice is its own update type that bypasses the DetectUploadFormat path entirely; the file-extension-based upload registry is for /api/sources/upload + tele.OnDocument paths only. NO real .ogg fixture in this story; voice handler doesn't decode the bytes — it just stores them via the sha256-dedupe source.Put. A02 will need a real fixture for the whisper round-trip; defer until then. HEADS-UP FOR A02 IMPLEMENTER (not this story's concern): after transcription succeeds in A02, original.ogg gets DELETED — voice memos are privacy-sensitive and the transcript supersedes them. A01 just stores; the purge is purely A02 territory. Don't add a TTL or cleanup job here; the simple atomic 'transcribed → purged' rule is enough.

userStories.title: Whisper HTTP client + voice_handler post-store transcription
userStories.description: Wire the aura-whisper sidecar (already running at WHISPER_BASE_URL=http://aura-whisper:8082, smoke-tested 2026-05-19) into the voice ingestion path. (a) internal/llm/whisper/client.go (NEW, ~150 LOC): Client struct {baseURL string; httpc *http.Client; logger *slog.Logger}. Constructor: New(baseURL string, timeout time.Duration, logger *slog.Logger) *Client. Method: Transcribe(ctx context.Context, audioBytes []byte, mimeType string, language string) (TranscribeResult, error). TranscribeResult struct {Text string; DurationS float64; ElapsedMs int}. Implementation: build multipart/form-data with file part (filename based on mimeType — voice.ogg / audio.wav / etc) + form fields {language, temperature=0.0, response_format=json}, POST to <baseURL>/inference, parse JSON {"text":"..."} from response body. Return error on non-200 (include status code + body excerpt; do NOT leak raw upstream body that may contain provider data — truncate to 200 chars). Timeout from constructor — default 60s is generous for 30s audio + cold start. (b) internal/llm/whisper/client_test.go: httptest server fixture returns canned JSON response; assert multipart body has correct file+language fields; assert timeout enforcement; assert error path on 500. (c) internal/config/config.go: add `WhisperBaseURL string` envconfig field with `envconfig:"WHISPER_BASE_URL" default:"http://aura-whisper:8082"` tag + `WhisperLanguage string` with `envconfig:"WHISPER_LANGUAGE" default:"it"` + `WhisperTimeoutSec int` with `envconfig:"WHISPER_TIMEOUT_SEC" default:"60"`. Wire whisper client construction in cmd/aura/helpers.go (or wherever doc-handler dependencies are built) so the Bot's voiceHandler receives a non-nil *whisper.Client. (d) internal/storage/sources/store/source.go: add TranscriptMeta struct {Text string; DurationS float64; ElapsedMs int; Language string} with json tags. Add `Transcript *TranscriptMeta` field to the Source struct (alongside the existing Extract pointer) with `json:"transcript,omitempty"`. (e) internal/telegram/voice_handler.go: extend process() — after a successful sources.Put, call whisper.Transcribe(ctx, oggBytes, "audio/ogg", cfg.WhisperLanguage). On success: write src_<id>/transcript.txt via the sources.Repository write-extra-file helper (look at how documents.go writes ocr.md alongside original — same shape via WriteExtractionFiles or a direct store.Write call); call sources.Update to set Status=StatusTranscribeComplete + Transcript=&meta. Then DELETE src_<id>/original.ogg via the store's helper (or os.Remove on the resolved path) — voice memos are privacy-sensitive and the transcript supersedes the raw audio. Set Source.OriginalDeletedAt = time.Now() on the Update so downstream code knows the binary is gone. Progress final message: '✅ Transcribed · src_xxx · <duration_s>s audio · <text-length> chars · audio purged · ready for Hub dispatch' (Hub dispatch wires in A03). On whisper failure: progress '❌ Transcription failed: <error>'; mark source Status=StatusFailed + Error=err.Error(); KEEP original.ogg on disk so the user can retry transcription later (only delete on success). Voice handler config gains a `Whisper *whisper.Client` field (nil = skip transcription, fall back to A01 behavior with progress '✅ Stored · ... · transcription disabled'). (f) internal/telegram/voice_handler_test.go: extend with httptest-mocked whisper server returning {"text":"ciao mondo prova"}; assert: transcript.txt is written with that exact text, original.ogg is REMOVED (os.Stat returns ErrNotExist), source.json Transcript field populated, Source.OriginalDeletedAt is non-zero, Status=StatusTranscribeComplete, progress text includes 'audio purged'.

Single atomic commit prefix: feat(audio): whisper HTTP client + voice transcription pipeline (US-MM-A02)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: read internal/telegram/documents.go in full (especially the call to WriteExtractionFiles + sources.Update at lines 263-275 — that's the pattern to mirror for transcript.txt write + Status flip). The whisper-server upstream HTTP shape is POST /inference (multipart with `file` field, form `language`, `temperature`, `response_format=json`) returning JSON `{"text":"transcript text here"}`. This was VERIFIED via curl during 2026-05-19 smoke test (commit 13ef9024). DO NOT invent a different shape — match the upstream server's contract exactly. DO NOT use whisper.cpp's CLI invocation pattern from docs/phase-mm-audio-plan-2026-05-17.md §3 — that document was written before Wave 1.5 picked the sidecar route. SCOPE: this story does NOT dispatch the transcript via the chat Hub — that's A03. After transcription, the user sees a Telegram message confirming the transcript is ready, but the assistant does NOT yet auto-respond to the transcript. A03 wires that. The TranscriptMeta has 4 fields (Text, DurationS, ElapsedMs, Language); DurationS comes from c.Message().Voice.Duration captured in onVoiceMessage before spawning the goroutine (pass as a `durationS int` param to process()). ElapsedMs comes from a t0 := time.Now() / time.Since() bracket around the Transcribe call. Language comes from cfg.WhisperLanguage (it default). Don't try to detect language client-side. The whisper-server upstream may return additional JSON fields (segments, language); the client parses only `text` for now — log the segments if present at debug level but don't store them (segment-time persistence is Phase-MM-EXTENDED per planning doc §5). DO NOT add a Groq/OpenAI Whisper API fallback — planning doc §3 lists it but Wave 2 keeps the surface minimal; the env-var seam (config.WhisperBaseURL) lets operators point at a different server if needed. PRIVACY/RETENTION INVARIANT: voice memos contain raw user audio (PII-equivalent). The Source store's normal pattern is to keep original.<ext> forever (PDFs, DOCXs, etc) — audio is the exception. After successful transcription the original.ogg is DELETED so only the transcript + source.json metadata remain. This is irreversible by design; if the user is unhappy with the transcript, they re-send the voice memo (SHA-dedupe will NOT kick in because the original is gone — new bytes will land in a new src_ id, which is correct). On transcription FAILURE the original is kept so the user can retry. Implementation note: use the source.Repository's existing path-resolving helper (grep for how documents.go reads back the file — there should be a Path(srcID, filename) or similar method) so the delete doesn't bypass the store abstraction. If no such helper exists today, ADD a small Remove(srcID, filename) method on the Repository interface — minimal addition, fits the existing read-extra/write-extra surface.

userStories.title: AfterTranscribeHook → chat Hub dispatch + E2E integration test
userStories.description: Wire the transcript into the agent loop as if the user had typed it. Pattern mirrors how docHandler's AfterOCRHook (documents.go:31-37) feeds OCR results to the ingest pipeline. (a) internal/telegram/voice_handler.go: add `AfterTranscribeHook func(ctx context.Context, src *source.Source, transcript string) error` type + field on voiceHandlerConfig and voiceHandler. Call hook after sources.Update sets StatusTranscribeComplete, BEFORE the final progress edit. On hook error: log warning at warn level, do NOT roll back the transcript file (it's durable); progress shows '✅ Transcribed · src_xxx · agent dispatch failed: <err>' so the user sees something happened but the assistant didn't reply. (b) cmd/aura/helpers.go (or wherever AfterOCRHook is wired for docHandler): construct an AfterTranscribeHook that builds a chat.InboundMessage with Channel=ChannelTelegram, PrincipalID=<sender id, same shape as OnText path>, ThreadID=<sender chat id>, Text=transcript, Attachments=[]chat.AttachmentRef{{SourceID: src.ID, MimeType: "audio/ogg", Status: "transcribe_complete"}}, Mode=DeliveryModeStreaming, CreatedAt=time.Now().UTC(), ChannelData (copy the Telegram context if available — the hook is called from inside the voice handler goroutine which has access to the original tele.Context via a captured closure). Dispatch via the chat.Hub the bot already holds (the same Hub that handles OnText messages). (c) The hook ALSO emits a final Telegram progress edit '✅ Transcribed · src_xxx · agent reply incoming…' so the user knows the transcript was accepted and the agent is running. The actual assistant reply arrives through the normal Telegram outbound progressive-edit path (no new code path needed — Hub dispatch goes through agent loop → OutboundEvent stream → existing telegramadapter outbound). (d) internal/telegram/voice_handler_e2e_test.go (NEW): integration test that wires a real voice handler with a mock chat.Hub (interface-based) + httptest-mocked whisper. Asserts: after process() completes, the mock Hub received an InboundMessage with Text==expected_transcript + Attachments[0].SourceID==stored_src_id + Channel==ChannelTelegram. (e) Probe coverage: DEFER — adding /api/test/voice_inbound dev endpoint is scope creep, and dev-only endpoints are an anti-pattern. Integration test in (d) covers the assertion. Document the deferral in the commit message; Wave 4 (web channel audio) gets probe coverage when /api/chat learns multipart audio.

Single atomic commit prefix: feat(audio): AfterTranscribeHook dispatches transcript as inbound message (US-MM-A03)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: read internal/telegram/documents.go AfterOCRHook usage (lines 31-37 + how it's invoked at line ~280) AND wherever cmd/aura/helpers.go (or app.go) builds the AfterOCRHook for the docHandler — that's the template. ALSO read internal/chat/types.go (InboundMessage has the fields A03 needs to populate — already shown in PRD context: ID, Channel, PrincipalID, ThreadID, Text, Attachments, Mode, CreatedAt, ChannelData) AND internal/chat/hub.go (or wherever the Dispatch method lives — grep for `func.*Hub.*Dispatch` and `Hub.RegisterInbound`). SCOPE: this story does NOT change the chat Hub or the agent loop — it only ADDs a new producer (voice handler) of InboundMessage. The agent loop processes it like any other text input. DO NOT add audio multipart support to /api/chat (that's Wave 4). The PrincipalID for the dispatched InboundMessage should match what the OnText path uses for the same Telegram user — grep for PrincipalID derivation in internal/channels/telegram/inbound.go (it's strconv.FormatInt(sender.ID, 10) — use the same shape). ChannelData: the OnText path stashes `tele_context` (telegramadapter.ChannelDataKeyContext) so the outbound adapter can edit the reply. For voice-initiated runs, we want the same behavior — the assistant's reply should appear in the same Telegram chat as the original voice memo. Pass the tele.Context captured in the voice handler's goroutine closure into ChannelData[ChannelDataKeyContext]. ANTIPATTERN GUARD: do NOT add a new chat.Channel value (no ChannelTelegramVoice — voice is still ChannelTelegram, just with an audio attachment). The discriminator is Attachments[0].MimeType, not Channel. PRINCIPLE: voice is just text-with-extra-context from the agent's POV; preserve that invariant.
